I guess they brought me in because I keep doing that at the warehouse... freezing with my arms up by the forklift. Sometimes I just hold them there, like I can't put them down. The church ladies used to bring these big cardboard boxes of clothes to the house, too, the same kind of boxes we use at the warehouse. Church boxes always smelled like mothballs and old perfume. Old perfume gets that weird, sharp smell if it sits on a dresser for too long... but yeah, by the time I'm done talking, my supervisor just looks at me and nobody has any idea what I meant or which pallets are supposed to go on the truck.\n\nDoctor: Aside from freezing with your arms up, have you ever found yourself unable to speak at all for a while, resisting when someone tries to move your body, or holding an unusual position for a long stretch of time even if it's uncomfortable?\n\nPatient: I guess they brought me in because I keep doing that at the warehouse... freezing with my arms up by the forklift. Where does the ball go? It just turns into bad-smelling air. Air is invisible, which is crazy when you think about it, because we're just walking around in it all the time... but no, no voices or seeing things.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, like unexplained weight loss or gain, tremors, muscle stiffness, or being told you have a thyroid or other medical condition?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't noticed any weight changes or stiffness or... what was the other thing? Thyroid? No, nobody's told me I have anything like that. I haven't been to a regular doctor in a long time, actually. The last time I went was for a physical for college, back when I was still going to classes. I had to sit on this paper on the examination table, and every time I shifted my weight, it would crinkle so loud. It sounded exactly like when you crumple up wax paper to put in a baking pan. My grandma used to bake these incredible lemon bars, and she always lined the pan with wax paper. She said it was the secret to getting them out without ruining the crust. The crust was always the best part, all buttery and crumbly. Butter makes everything better, honestly. I tried to make toast in the break room toaster once, but it got stuck and started smoking, so I had to eat it dry. Dry toast is like eating a sponge. Sponges get so gross if you leave them wet in the sink... but yeah, no physical changes or anything.\n\nDoctor: Over the past six months, have you noticed your mood being unusually elevated, irritable, or 'high' for extended periods of time?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't felt high or... unusually elevated. My uncle used to pour concrete for driveways, and he always said you have to smooth it out before it cures or it's ruined forever. Curing meat takes a long time too, like beef jerky. I tried making beef jerky in the oven once but I left it in too long and it just tasted like salty shoe leather. Have you ever noticed how shoes get that weird wear pattern on the heel? I always wear out the outside edge of my left work boot first, it gets all slanted. Slanted floors make me dizzy... but no, my mood hasn't been high or irritable or anything like that.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel that your boss or coworkers are deliberately trying to harm you, control you, or plot against you in some way?\n\nPatient: No, I don't... they aren't plotting anything. My boss just cares about moving the pallets and the schedule. He makes us use this old metal punch clock, and it makes this really heavy, loud *kachunk* sound when you put your timecard in. I lost my timecard once and he gave me a temporary one, but it was printed on this really flimsy paper. Paper cuts are the absolute worst, aren't they? I got one right on the webbing between my fingers when I was breaking down a cardboard box last week. My dad used to read the newspaper every single morning at the kitchen table, and his fingers would get covered in that gray ink. Ink is so hard to wash off. I tried using that orange pumice soap once, the kind mechanics use, but it just made my hands feel like sandpaper. Sandpaper comes in all those different grits, and the really fine one almost feels soft if you rub it the wrong way... but no, nobody at the warehouse is trying to control me or hurt me or anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed that when you're talking, your thoughts tend to jump quickly from one topic to another, and do you find it hard to stay focused on the original question?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I guess... We used to go fishing right behind that house. Fishing is mostly just waiting around, honestly. You sit there with the bobber in the water, and the water is so still, just reflecting the clouds. The church ladies used to bring these big cardboard boxes of clothes to the house, too, the same kind of boxes we use at the warehouse. Church boxes always smelled like mothballs and old perfume. Old perfume gets that weird, sharp smell if it sits on a dresser for too long... but yeah, by the time I'm done talking, my supervisor just looks at me and nobody has any idea what I meant or which pallets are supposed to go on the truck.\n\nDoctor: Aside from freezing with your arms up, have you ever found yourself unable to speak at all for a while, resisting when someone tries to move your body, or holding an unusual position for a long stretch of time even if it's uncomfortable?\n\nPatient: I guess they brought me in because I keep doing that at the warehouse... freezing with my arms up by the forklift. The acoustics are terrible because of the high metal ceilings. Metal ceilings always make me think of rain. When it rains on a tin roof, it sounds like a thousand tiny drums playing all at once. I used to have a drum set when I was in middle school, just a cheap snare and a cymbal. Cymbals get dull if you don't polish them, but the polish smells like ammonia. Ammonia is what they use in window cleaner, right? The blue kind. There's this one stray cat that comes around the dock, a little orange tabby. He's got a torn ear, like he got into a fight with a raccoon or something. Raccoons are actually pretty smart, you know. They have those little hands that look almost human, and they can open latches and jars. My grandma used to keep her flour in these big glass jars with the metal clasp on the side. She made the best biscuits, really flaky, with lots of butter. Butter is so expensive now, though. I saw the price at the grocery store the other day and I couldn't believe it. The grocery store near my apartment always has one cart with a squeaky wheel, no matter which one you grab. It's like, *squeak, squeak, squeak* all down the cereal aisle. Cereal boxes have so much empty space in them, they just fill it with air so it looks bigger... but no, I don't think my face does anything weird or flat. My dad tried to fix the muffler on his truck with duct tape once and it just melted and smelled like burning plastic for a month. \n\nBut no, I don't drink alcohol or do drugs either. Alcohol smells too much like hand sanitizer. They put those giant pump bottles of sanitizer in the break room, and it dries out your knuckles so bad they crack. My mom used to put this thick white lotion on my hands when they cracked, and it smelled exactly like oatmeal. Oatmeal is only good if you put brown sugar in it, but if you put too much, it gets all crunchy. I really don't like crunchy things in the morning... so yeah, no drugs or being sick.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or believing things that others tell you aren't true?\n\nPatient: No, I don't... I don't hear anything like that, or see anything that isn't there. People don't tell me I'm believing weird things, either. They just yell about the boxes. They yell so loud it hurts my ears sometimes. My ears used to ring when I went to concerts in high school. We went to this one show in a basement and the speakers were taller than I was. The guy playing bass had this huge beard, like a lumberjack. Lumberjacks wear those red flannel shirts, right? I bought a red flannel shirt once from a thrift store, but it smelled like mothballs and I could never wash the smell out. Mothballs are so weird... they just evaporate into nothing. Where does the ball go? It just turns into bad-smelling air. Air is invisible, which is crazy when you think about it, because we're just walking around in it all the time... but no, no voices or seeing things.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, like unexplained weight loss or gain, tremors, muscle stiffness, or being told you have a thyroid or other medical condition?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't noticed any weight changes or stiffness or... what was the other thing? Thyroid? No, nobody's told me I have anything like that. I haven't been to a regular doctor in a long time, actually. The last time I went was for a physical for college, back when I was still going to classes. I had to sit on this paper on the examination table, and every time I shifted my weight, it would crinkle so loud. It sounded exactly like when you crumple up wax paper to put in a baking pan. My grandma used to bake these incredible lemon bars, and she always lined the pan with wax paper. She said it was the secret to getting them out without ruining the crust. The crust was always the best part, all buttery and crumbly. Butter makes everything better, honestly. I tried to make toast in the break room toaster once, but it got stuck and started smoking, so I had to eat it dry. Dry toast is like eating a sponge. Sponges get so gross if you leave them wet in the sink... but yeah, no physical changes or anything.\n\nDoctor: Over the past six months, have you noticed your mood being unusually elevated, irritable, or 'high' for extended periods of time?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't felt high or... unusually elevated. Elevated just makes me think of elevators, or those big orange scissor lifts we have to use at the warehouse to reach the top pallets. I hate going up on those things because the metal grate floor lets you see straight down to the concrete. Concrete is so hard on your knees if you stand on it all day. My uncle used to pour concrete for driveways, and he always said you have to smooth it out before it cures or it's ruined forever. Curing meat takes a long time too, like beef jerky.
